title: Realizing an intermediate field as a compatible proper smooth curve factorization
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $X,Y$ be smooth proper integral $k$-curves of dimension one [def-sc-curves], [def-pc-integral-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a nonconstant $k$-morphism, meaning that it does not factor through a $k$-rational point of $Y$. Put $L=k(X)$ and $K=k(Y)$ [def-sc-function-field], and identify $K$ with its image in $L$ under $f^*$. For any intermediate field $K\subseteq E\subseteq L$ [def-pc-field-extension], the extensions $E/K$ and $L/E$ are finite [def-pc-field-tower], and $E/k$ is finitely generated of transcendence degree one [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. There exist a smooth proper integral $k$-curve $Z$ of dimension one, a $k$-isomorphism $\theta:k(Z)\xrightarrow{\sim}E$, and nonconstant $k$-morphisms $a:X\to Z$ and $b:Z\to Y$ such that
$$f=b\circ a,\qquad a^*=\iota_{E,L}\circ\theta,\qquad b^*=\theta^{-1}\circ\iota_{K,E},$$
where $\iota$ denotes the indicated field inclusions. In particular, these maps identify the induced extensions $k(X)/a^*k(Z)$ and $k(Z)/b^*k(Y)$ with $L/E$ and $E/K$, respectively.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proper-curve-function-field-morphisms] to $X,Y,f$. Its hypotheses are exactly our algebraically closed base, smooth proper integral curves of dimension one, and nonconstancy. Thus $f^*$ is a $k$-embedding, $L/K$ is finite, and $K/k,L/k$ are finitely generated of transcendence degree one. After the stipulated identification of $K$ with its image, apply [lem-sfb-finite-field-tower-intermediate] to $K\subseteq E\subseteq L$; this proves finiteness of $E/K$ and $L/E$.

proof.text: Write $K=k(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$, and choose a finite $K$-spanning family $e_1,\ldots,e_s$ of $E$, which exists by [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] and step 1. The subfield $k(t_1,\ldots,t_r,e_1,\ldots,e_s)$ contains every sum $\sum_i c_i e_i$ with $c_i\in K$, hence equals $E$. Therefore $E/k$ is finitely generated.

source.place: Tag 0BU1 (fields-lemma-finite-finitely-generated), proof, applied to E/K and combined with generators of K/k.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], applied to the finite-dimensional $E$-algebra $L$, every element of $L$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $E$; over a field such a polynomial is nonzero. Thus $L/E$ is algebraic. Apply [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower] to $k\subseteq E\subseteq L$: $\operatorname{trdeg}_E L=0$ and $1=\operatorname{trdeg}_kL=\operatorname{trdeg}_kE+0$, so $\operatorname{trdeg}_kE=1$.

proof.text: Apply the existence clause of [lem-trf-algclosed-curve-model] to the algebraically closed field $k$ and the extension $E/k$ just shown finitely generated of transcendence degree one. It supplies a smooth proper integral finite-type $k$-scheme $Z$ of dimension one and a $k$-isomorphism $\theta:k(Z)\xrightarrow{\sim}E$. Properness includes separatedness, so this is a curve in [def-sc-curves]. The additional valuation-ring clause of the cited node is not needed.

proof.text: The maps $\alpha=\iota_{E,L}\circ\theta:k(Z)\hookrightarrow L$ and $\beta=\theta^{-1}\circ\iota_{K,E}:K\hookrightarrow k(Z)$ are $k$-embeddings, since each inclusion and $\theta$ preserve $k$. The surjectivity of the correspondence in [lem-sfb-proper-curve-function-field-morphisms], first for $(X,Z)$ and then for $(Z,Y)$, gives nonconstant $k$-morphisms $a:X\to Z$ and $b:Z\to Y$ with $a^*=\alpha$ and $b^*=\beta$. All three curves satisfy that correspondence hypotheses by the original assumptions and step 4.

source.place: Tag 0CD2 (curves-proposition-unwind-morphism-smooth), proof: intermediate-field factorization, expanded using Tag 0BY1 (curves-theorem-curves-rational-maps) and Tag 0BY3 (curves-lemma-nonsingular-model-smooth).

proof.text: First $b\circ a$ is nonconstant: both maps send generic point to generic point by [lem-sfb-proper-curve-function-field-morphisms]. If their composite factored through a $k$-point $y:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$, then $y$ would map to the generic point of $Y$. The residue-field homomorphism of [def-weil-residue-field] would therefore give a $k$-embedding $K\hookrightarrow k$. For each $x\in K$, subtract its scalar image in $k$; injectivity forces $x$ to equal that scalar in $K$, so $K=k$, contradicting $\operatorname{trdeg}_kK=1$. Now the composition clause of [lem-sfb-proper-curve-function-field-morphisms] applies and gives $(b\circ a)^*=a^*\circ b^*=\iota_{E,L}\circ\theta\circ\theta^{-1}\circ\iota_{K,E}=\iota_{K,L}=f^*$. Injectivity of that correspondence for $(X,Y)$ gives $b\circ a=f$. Finally $a^*k(Z)=E$ inside $L$, and $\theta(b^*K)=K$ inside $E$; the identity on $L$ and $\theta$ identify the stated extensions with $L/E$ and $E/K$, respectively.

lean.statement: theorem exists_curve_intermediate_field_realization (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (sY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y] [IsCurve sX] [IsCurve sY] [Smooth sX] [Smooth sY] [IsProper sX] [IsProper sY] (hXdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) (hYdim : topologicalKrullDim Y = 1) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (hf_nonconstant : ¬ ∃ y : Spec (.of k) ⟶ Y, y ≫ sY = 𝟙 _ ∧ sX ≫ y = f) : ∃ hfη : f (genericPoint X) = genericPoint Y, ∀ (E : Type u) [Field E] (i : Y.functionField →+* E) (j : E →+* X.functionField), j.comp i = (f.functionFieldMap hfη).hom → @Module.Finite Y.functionField E _ _ (@Algebra.toModule _ _ _ _ i.toAlgebra) ∧ @Module.Finite E X.functionField _ _ (@Algebra.toModule _ _ _ _ j.toAlgebra) ∧ @IntermediateField.FG k _ E _ (i.comp sY.curveFunctionFieldBaseMap).toAlgebra ⊤ ∧ @Algebra.trdeg k E _ _ (i.comp sY.curveFunctionFieldBaseMap).toAlgebra = 1 ∧ ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (sZ : Z ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (_ : IsIntegral Z) (θ : Z.functionField ≃+* E) (a : X ⟶ Z) (b : Z ⟶ Y), IsCurve sZ ∧ Smooth sZ ∧ IsProper sZ ∧ topologicalKrullDim Z = 1 ∧ θ.toRingHom.comp sZ.curveFunctionFieldBaseMap = i.comp sY.curveFunctionFieldBaseMap ∧ a ≫ sZ = sX ∧ b ≫ sY = sZ ∧ a ≫ b = f ∧ (¬ ∃ z : Spec (.of k) ⟶ Z, z ≫ sZ = 𝟙 _ ∧ sX ≫ z = a) ∧ (¬ ∃ y : Spec (.of k) ⟶ Y, y ≫ sY = 𝟙 _ ∧ sZ ≫ y = b) ∧ ∃ (haη : a (genericPoint X) = genericPoint Z) (hbη : b (genericPoint Z) = genericPoint Y), (a.functionFieldMap haη).hom = j.comp θ.toRingHom ∧ (b.functionFieldMap hbη).hom = θ.symm.toRingHom.comp i ∧ (a.functionFieldMap haη).hom.fieldRange = j.fieldRange ∧ (b.functionFieldMap hbη).hom.fieldRange.map θ.toRingHom = i.fieldRange
lean.note: Intermediate fields are represented by field embeddings i : k(Y) →+* E and j : E →+* k(X) whose composite is the actual generic-stalk map of f. Their injectivity is automatic for fields. The k-algebra on E is explicitly the composite of i with the canonical scalar map of Y. The final range identities express both induced extension identifications.
